title: Interacting non-Hermitian edge and cluster bursts on a digital quantum processor
task: Simulate interacting non-Hermitian systems on a quantum processor
key_results: Observed edge-burst signatures in 64-unit-cell systems; identified interaction-driven cluster bursts and dissipative-gap closing on superconducting processor
comments: This work effectively demonstrates that digital quantum processors can handle demanding non-Hermitian simulations with tunable interactions, though scaling to larger systems remains limited.

model_io.model: Superconducting quantum processor with digital non-Hermitian simulation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dissipation drives edge-burst phenomena in interacting multi-particle systems
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via observation of spatially extended and patterned edge bursts

title: Nonlinear reversal of photoexcitation on the attosecond time scale improves ultrafast X-ray diffraction images
task: Reverse photoexcitation damage in X-ray diffraction via sub-femtosecond pulses
key_results: Sub-fs pulses enhance X-ray diffraction and reduce energy absorption vs. 15-fs pulses; Rabi-like dynamics suppress electronic bleaching; improved nanoscale imaging feasibility demonstrated
comments: The attosecond control of X-ray damage is innovative, but applicability depends on availability of sub-fs X-ray sources, limiting near-term impact.

model_io.model: X-ray diffraction of neon nanoparticles with variable pulse duration

hypotheses.hypothesis: Sub-fs pulses enable stimulated emission and Rabi-like dynamics to suppress damage
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via enhanced diffraction and reduced bleaching

title: Observation of a relativistic analog of the Brewster effect in electron-photon scattering
task: Observe relativistic Brewster effect in electron-photon scattering
key_results: Demonstrated angle-dependent suppression of forward photon emission for in-plane polarization; Lorentz-transform predictions validated; identified polarization as controllable degree of freedom
comments: The observation elegantly connects classical optics to relativistic regimes, though practical applications in light-matter control remain speculative.

model_io.model: High-brightness relativistic electron beam with optical laser

hypotheses.hypothesis: Relativistic scattering exhibits Brewster-like suppression angle
hypotheses.result: Confirmed experimentally for in-plane polarization

title: Function-specific epistasis shapes evolutionary trajectories towards antibiotic resistance
task: Characterize function-specific epistasis driving antibiotic resistance evolution
key_results: Resistance evolution highly repeatable along common path in most backgrounds; function-specific epistasis causes deviations; disrupting specific cellular functions slows resistance evolution for select drugs
comments: The robotic evolution experiments are rigorous and the function-specific framing is insightful for drug development, though mechanistic understanding of which functions matter for which drugs remains incomplete.

model_io.model: Robotic evolution platform with E. coli under antibiotic selection

hypotheses.hypothesis: Global epistasis predicts most resistance trajectories
hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed; common path observed but minority deviations indicate function-specific effects dominate in some cases

hypotheses.hypothesis: Disrupting specific cellular functions alters drug-specific evolutionary pathways
hypotheses.result: Confirmed across three clinically relevant antibiotics and hundreds of gene-deletion strains

hypotheses.hypothesis: Function-specific epistasis often slows resistance evolution
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; small-molecule inhibitors of identified targets recapitulate effects

title: Superconductivity under pressure in a van der Waals heavy-fermion metal
task: Map pressure-dependent phase diagram of heavy-fermion superconductor CeSiI
key_results: Tc(AFM) suppressed by pressure; superconducting dome emerges with max Tc ≈ 240 mK; Kondo coherence shows V-shaped pressure dependence; large upper critical field indicates unconventional pairing
comments: The work provides compelling evidence for unconventional superconductivity in a 2D heavy-fermion system, though the pairing mechanism remains unidentified.

model_io.model: CeSiI heavy-fermion system under hydrostatic pressure

hypotheses.hypothesis: Suppression of antiferromagnetism promotes superconductivity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via emergence of superconducting dome at AFM suppression

hypotheses.hypothesis: Kondo coherence exhibits non-monotonic pressure dependence
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via V-shaped Tc(p) behavior

title: RadCube MAGIC observations of complex field aligned currents associated with a supersubstorm during the May 2024 geomagnetic storm
task: Map field-aligned currents during supersubstorm via CubeSat magnetometer
key_results: Resolved detailed FAC structure during May 2024 supersubstorm; observed magnetic fluctuations across broad spatial/temporal scales; demonstrated need for dense LEO magnetometer constellations
comments: The RadCube observations provide useful FAC detail, but a single CubeSat offers limited spatial coverage; the conclusion about constellation requirements is more aspirational than demonstrative.

model_io.model: MAGIC magnetometer on RadCube CubeSat during geomagnetic storm

hypotheses.hypothesis: Supersubstorms produce structured FACs with localized current spikes
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via in-situ measurements showing magnetic fluctuations across multiple scales

title: Dual-band dual-beam millimeter-wave antenna using dual circular microstrip rings
task: Design compact dual-band dual-beam millimeter-wave antenna
key_results: Operating bands 24.2–30 GHz and 32.5–43.5 GHz; dual beams at ±40° and ±24°; peak realized gain 9 dBi at 38 GHz, >6 dBi across both bands
comments: The antenna achieves impressive performance without vias or metamaterials, making it practical for integration, though the lack of novelty in the underlying physics limits impact.

model_io.model: Dual circular-ring microstrip antenna with optimization

hypotheses.hypothesis: Higher-order resonant modes enable dual-band dual-beam operation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed through simulation and measurement

title: Real-space observation of the temporal evolution of nanoscale mechanical heterogeneities in deeply aged polymer glasses
task: Observe nanoscale mechanical heterogeneity evolution in aged polymer glass
key_results: Modulus variations persist ~70 K below Tg at slow, localized rates; contrasts with fast cooperative changes near Tg; suggests correlation with faster-than-α-relaxation process
comments: The bimodal AFM approach provides valuable real-space evidence for theoretical predictions, though connecting NMH dynamics quantitatively to α-relaxation remains incomplete.

model_io.model: Bimodal atomic force microscopy of epoxy glass under aging

hypotheses.hypothesis: Localized configurational rearrangements persist deep in glassy state
hypotheses.result: Confirmed via observation of persistent modulus variations at 70 K below Tg

title: Anti-malaria antibody engineering broadens recognition motifs and reveals new homotypic interactions that enhance protective breadth
task: Engineer monoclonal antibodies with broadened recognition of malaria circumsporozoite protein variants
key_results: L9_yd19 variant maintains potency against benchmark strain while improving protection against rare strains with altered repeat spacing; cryo-EM reveals dual homotypic interfaces enabling asymmetric trimeric and head-to-head dimeric antibody layers
comments: The discovery of dual symmetry elements (2-fold and asymmetric 3-fold) providing structural breadth is mechanistically elegant, though in vivo efficacy improvement was modest.

model_io.model: Site saturation mutagenesis and yeast display screening
inputs: PfCSP variants with altered NVDP/NANP repeat patterns

model_io.model: Cryo-EM structural analysis

hypotheses.hypothesis: Improved affinity to minor repeats enhances protection against rare parasite strains with altered repeat spacing
hypotheses.result: L9_yd19 showed modest improvement against two-repeat strain while retaining benchmark potency

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dual homotypic symmetry enables recognition of diverse PfCSP architectures
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by cryo-EM; two distinct interfaces combine into asymmetric trimers and head-to-head dimers

title: Human cortex organizes dynamic co-fluctuations along the sensorimotor-association axis
task: Characterize how brain hierarchical architecture emerges from amplitude-dependent neural co-fluctuations
key_results: Sensorimotor networks dominate high-amplitude states, associative systems intermediate-amplitude, and limbic systems low-amplitude co-fluctuations; hierarchy refined from childhood to adulthood
comments: Elegant demonstration that static network architecture can be understood as a dynamic cascade across amplitude regimes, bridging timescales from milliseconds to development.

model_io.model: fMRI time-series analysis with amplitude stratification
inputs: resting-state and naturalistic fMRI BOLD signals from 4 independent datasets

hypotheses.hypothesis: Brain hierarchical architecture is preserved through structured amplitude-dependent cascades of co-fluctuations
hypotheses.result: Confirmed across multiple datasets; hierarchy exhibited developmental refinement and adaptive reconfiguration under naturalistic stimuli
